key_concepts: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the core language used to structure and display content on the web, defining elements like text, images, links, and page layout so browsers can render websites properly.

CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets. It is a stylesheet language used to style and enhance website presentation. CSS is one of the three main components of a webpage, along with HTML and JavaScript.

JavaScript is a programming language used to create dynamic content for websites. It is a lightweight, cross-platform, and single-threaded programming language. It's an interpreted language that executes code line by line, providing more flexibility.
HTTP stands for Hypertext Transfer Protocol, and it’s the system that allows communication between web browsers (like Google Chrome or Firefox) andweb servers.
The Domain Name System (DNS) is a hierarchical and distributed naming system that translates human-readable domain names into IP addresses, enabling users to access websites easily.
A REST API (Representational State Transfer API) enables communication between client and server over HTTP. It exchanges data typically in JSON format using standard web protocols.
The TCP/IP model is a layered networking framework that explains how data is communicated between devices over a network using standardized protocols to ensure reliable and efficient transmission.

topic_title: WebSocket and Its Difference from HTTP
key_concepts: HTTP and WebSocket are both ways for computers to talk to each other, but they work in different ways. HTTP is used for simple requests, like when you load a webpage, where the computer sends a request and the server replies, then the connection is closed. WebSocket keeps the connection open, allowing for real-time, two-way communication, making it great for things like live chats or online games where constant updates are needed.
